chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr al-Arjani; and my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Zurara, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:

I accompanied Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a Hajj journey. In a long hadith, I asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, if the grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) were to be disinterred, would anything be found in it?' He said, 'O son of Bukayr, how great are your questions! Verily, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is with his father, his mother, and his brother in the house of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with him they are provided for and enriched. And verily, he is hanging on the right side of the Throne, clinging to it, saying: 'O my Lord, fulfill for me what You have promised me.' And verily, he looks at those who visit him, and he knows them better, and their names, and the names of their fathers, and that which is in their saddles, better than one of them knows his own son. And verily, he looks at those who weep for him, so he seeks forgiveness for them and asks his father for forgiveness for them. And he says to the weeper: 'O you who weep, if you knew what Allah has prepared for you, you would be happier than you are grieved.' And verily, he seeks forgiveness for them for every sin and every mistake.'

key_terms.يَمِينِ الْعَرْشِ: the right side of the Throne

ai.seo_question: What is the state of Imam al-Husayn's grave and his interaction with visitors according to Kamil al-Ziyarat?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elucidates the concept of *Barzakh* by affirming that al-Husayn (a.s.) remains physically present in his grave, alive and sustained by divine provision, while maintaining a unique spiritual proximity to the Throne. The text highlights the intercessory role of the Imam, who not only recognizes individual visitors by name but also actively seeks forgiveness for them, transforming the act of weeping into a source of profound joy and divine reward.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. My father narrated to me from Ḥusain ibn Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Ḥusain ibn Sa’īd, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Asam, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Bukayr Al-Arjāni, who said:

I accompanied Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) (from Madīnah to Makkah) on a Hajj trip and I asked him, “O son of the Messenger of Allāh! If the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) was to be disinterred, would anything be found in it?” Imam (a.s.) replied: O son of Bukayr! Your questions are (always) about great matters. Verily Ḥusain (a.s.) along with his father, mother, and his brother (a.s.) are with the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) in his house and they are being rewarded and sustained, (just) as the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) is. Verily Ḥusain (a.s.) is hanging on to the right side of the Throne and he says, “O my Lord! Fulfill Your promise to me.” Verily Ḥusain (a.s.) looks at those who go to his Ziyārah and he knows them and he knows their names, the names of their fathers, and that which they carry along with them even better than they know their own sons. Verily he looks at those who cry over him and he seeks forgiveness for them and asks his father (a.s.) to seek forgiveness for them. And he says to them (those who cry over him), “O those who cry (over me)! If you knew about that which Allāh has prepared for you, you would be more happy than you are grieved (over me).” Imam (a.s.) continued, “Verily Ḥusain (a.s.) seeks forgiveness for them for every sin and for every mistake.” The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Zurārah, from ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Asam, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Bukayr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
